subject.title: feat: add jsonl support to memory indexer

question: Should builtin memorySearch.extraPaths support arbitrary `.jsonl` files, or should raw message logs stay in the existing session-memory, QMD, converter, or plugin path?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing native JSONL ingestion changes memory file format scope and the sensitive local-log trust boundary.

options.title: Approve a narrow JSONL design
options.body: Define the accepted JSONL shape, line-to-chunk mapping, read behavior, watcher handling, docs, and security limits before implementation.

options.title: Document the supported alternative
options.body: Keep builtin extraPaths Markdown/multimodal-only and document QMD, session transcript indexing, or a converter/plugin workflow for raw logs.

options.title: Defer to memory plugin API work
options.body: Treat arbitrary raw-log ingestion as part of a broader memory plugin/file-ingestion API rather than expanding builtin memory now.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow JSONL design
recommendation.body: Define the accepted JSONL shape, line-to-chunk mapping, read behavior, watcher handling, docs, and security limits before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing issue discussion and related memory API reviews point to steipete as the strongest routing candidate for this product/security scope choice.
